{{Short description|Swiss mathematician (1878–1959)}}
[[File: Picone Franel Dandliker Kraitchik Kollros Wolff Straszewicz Zurich1932.tif|thumb|Louis Kollros (3rd from right) at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] 1932 in Zürich]]
'''Louis Kollros''' (7 May 1878 – 19 June 1959) was a Swiss mathematician. From 1909 to 1948 he was a professor ordinarius of [[geometry]] at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name=Stammbach>{{cite web|author=Stammbach, Urs|authorlink=Urs Stammbach|title=Kollros, Louis|website=Dictionnaire historique de la Suisse|date=31 March 2009|url=http://www.hls-dhs-dss.ch/textes/f/F43123.php}}</ref>

==Biography==
Kollros was born on 7 May 1878 in [[La Chaux-de-Fonds]]. Kollros, the son of a baker, was from 1896 as a student of mathematics and physics at the [[ETH Zurich|Zurich Polytechnikum]], where he was a fellow student of [[Albert Einstein]] and [[Marcel Grossmann]].<ref>At that time there were parallel lectures in German and French. Kollros attended only the French lectures, as he mentions in his reminiscences published (in connection with a celebration held in Bern) for the 50th anniversary in 1955 of the theory of special relativity. Louis Kollros: ''Albert Einstein en Suisse: Souvenirs.'' In: ''Helvetica Physica Acta.'' Supplementum 4, 1956, pp. 271-281, and as a German translation: ''Erinnerungen eines Kommilitonen.'' In: [[Carl Seelig]] (ed.): ''Helle Zeit – dunkle Zeit: In memoriam Albert Einstein.'' Europa Verlag, Zürich 1956, pp. 17–31 {{doi|10.1007/978-3-322-84225-1_3}}</ref> After graduating in 1900, Kollros taught mathematics from 1900 to 1909 in secondary school in his hometown  of La Chaux-de-Fonds. In 1903–1904 to 1909 he studied in Göttingen with [[Hermann Minkowski]] and [[David Hilbert]]. From 1904 to 1909 Kollross was a ''privat-docent'' (lecturer) at the [[University of Neuchâtel]]. He received his doctorate in 1905 from the [[University of Zurich]] with thesis advisor Hermann Minkowski and thesis ''Un algorithme pour l'approximation simultaneé de deux grandeurs''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=57094}}</ref> At ETH Zurich, where Marcel Grossmann taught until 1927 in the same field, Kollross held from 1909 to 1948 the francophone chair of ''géométrie descriptive et de géométrie euclidienne''.<ref name=Stammbach/>

In 1940–1941 he was president of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]] and from 1958 an honorary member of the Society.<ref>{{cite web|title=Honorary Members of the SMS|url=http://math.ch/members/honorary-members}}</ref> He was president of the [[Jakob Steiner|Steiner]]-[[Ludwig Schläfli|Schläfli]] committee (tasked with the publication of their works). In this role, he was co-editor of Schläfli's collected works (3 vols.,1950–1956).<ref name=Stammbach/>

He wrote biographies of [[Évariste Galois]] (1949, 24 p.) and Jakob Steiner (1947, 24 p.), which appeared in the supplements to the ''[[Elemente der Mathematik]]'' ([[Birkhäuser Verlag]]).<ref name=Stammbach/>

His doctoral students include [[Ferdinand Gonseth]].

He died on 19 June 1959 in [[Zürich]].

==Selected publications==
* [http://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/008855738 ''Un algorithme pour l'approximation simultaneé de deux grandeurs''], Imprimerie Soullier, Geneva 1905
* ''Géométrie descriptive'', Orell Füssli, Zürich 1918
* ''Cours de géométrie projective'', Griffon, Neuchâtel 1946, 108 p.
